title: sse: fix partial-JSON delimiter ordering and token/event framing
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Context: Users and our internal e2e tests observed corrupted partial JSON payloads and invalid OpenAI-compat event ordering when streaming tokens+events over SSE. Root cause: a race between the chunking/flushing path and the SSE framing layer where delimiters (partial-json boundary markers) were emitted independently of token/event emission, causing delimiter events to be delivered out-of-order relative to partial-token events. This surfaced when function_call streaming and structured output were enabled together (token events interleaved with delimiter markers).

This PR: implements an explicit delimiter queue and strict emission ordering in the SSE framing layer so that delimiter markers and token/event frames are sequenced deterministically. Changes include: (1) a small refactor of framing.go to centralize frame emission; (2) an in-memory delimiter queue that is drained in the framing goroutine to preserve relative ordering with token/event frames; (3) updates to the OpenAI-compatibility layer to emit start/end/partial function_call tokens as token events rather than separate delimiter-only frames; (4) added fuzz and regression tests covering chunk boundaries, partial JSON tokens, and mixed token/event interleaving; (5) minor TS/Python SDK parser compatibility tests to ensure no breaking client behavior.

Notes: the change preserves backwards compatibility for clients that expect delimiter events, but orders them predictably. A follow-up will expose a config toggle for legacy clients to preserve previous best-effort ordering (ENG-4823 follow-up).

conversation: Diego Ramos (reviewer): I'm seeing the framing refactor — can you add a short note describing the buffer invariants and the ordering guarantee? It's important for future maintainers.
Aisha Patel (author): Added comments in framing.go and a brief section in openai_compat/README.md explaining invariants and ordering guarantees.

Lina Chen (reviewer): Tests look good. The fuzz test uncovered a rare edge-case where a delimiter + zero-length token pair could be coalesced by the earlier batching logic. Did you consider the impact on batching throughput?

Aisha Patel (author): Yes — I added a microbenchmark (benchmarks/sse_ordering_bench.go) and measured <2% median throughput impact for typical workloads. Added opt-in config for legacy ordering in a follow-up to avoid expanding this PR further.
